claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS only, and multi-cloud with CDK is nearly impossible.
AWS CDK allowed developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python, while Pulumi supports any programming language.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because CloudFormation is slower than Pulumi's direct execution.
AWS CDK secrets management is limited to AWS Secrets Manager only.
AWS CDK state is a CloudFormation state file, whereas Pulumi state is Pulumi-managed.
CDK and CloudFormation generate an intermediary format (YAML or JSON) that is then executed to deploy resources.
Pulumi supports defining infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C#, and deploying to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: 'With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle.'
SST Ion is the code name for a new engine deploying SST applications using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi Insights product page provides improved visibility and debugging capabilities.
Pulumi has built-in extensibility features such as custom providers and dynamic components.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS simplifies 'day one' tasks, documented in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure in a single sst.config.ts file.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; the team began the Ion rewrite in late 2023.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's 'Moving away from CDK' blog says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'
SST's 'Moving away from CDK' blog says that when you run sst deploy, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine which calls the bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'

SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and others, and a Pulumiverse Vercel provider (@pulumi/aws, cloudflare, command, docker-build, random, tls, @pulumiverse/vercel).
The SST repository is now anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs pulumi up; Defang and Nitric run deployments through the Pulumi engine.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly with Pulumi and deployed in the same SST app.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package had roughly 796,000 (796,291) weekly downloads for September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent, which has a larger GitHub following than SST.
SST's release cadence and Pulumi engine dependency haven't changed since opencode.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components exist as Pulumi offerings usable with the same engine SST uses.
Linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
